title: The World Trade Organization
text: The World Trade Organization (WTO) is an intergovernmental organization that regulates and facilitates international trade between nations. It was established on January 1, 1995, replacing the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT). The WTO provides a framework for negotiating trade agreements, resolving trade disputes, and monitoring compliance with WTO agreements. As of 2023, it has 164 member countries, accounting for over 98% of world trade. The WTO operates on principles including most-favored-nation (MFN) treatment and national treatment. Critics argue that WTO rules can disadvantage developing nations and prioritize trade liberalization over labor and environmental standards.
